name: Tapo P110M (EU)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11b/g/n). The EU datasheet says Bluetooth is used for setup only.

matter.note: TP-Link's EU pages call it Matter-certified. The CSA listing (family SKU P110M, cert CSA23546MAT41059-24) names only the P110M(UK) variant; we found no CSA entry naming P110M(EU).

apple_home.note: TP-Link lists Apple Home. There is no HomeKit (HAP) mode, so this goes through Matter; the EU datasheet says a controller such as an Apple TV or HomePod is needed.

google_home.note: Added in the Google Home app by scanning the Matter code. Needs a Google Matter controller.

alexa.note: TP-Link says Matter-enabled Tapo devices connect to Alexa directly through Matter, not through the Tapo skill. Needs an Echo that works as a Matter controller.

smartthings.note: TP-Link lists Samsung SmartThings; setup is through Matter.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the P110M among supported Tapo plugs; newer devices need your TP-Link account credentials once. It can also be added through the Matter integration.

hubRequired.note: The EU datasheet says no hub is needed with the Tapo app; third-party apps need a Matter controller.

localControl.note: TP-Link's EU pages say Tapo Matter devices talk to other certified devices on the local network (LAN). This is a Matter statement; we found no EU page on Tapo-app control without internet.

energyMonitoring.note: Real-time and historical use plus bill estimates in the Tapo app. Firmware 1.3.2 (2025) added Matter energy reporting; TP-Link names SmartThings and Home Assistant as the platforms verified to show it.

maxLoadWatts.note: 16 A / 3680 W for general use and resistive loads; 1/6 HP motor.

summary: Matter is how the EU Tapo P110M reaches Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings, while Home Assistant can use either its TP-Link integration or Matter. The Tapo app needs no hub, but each third-party platform needs its own Matter controller. It's a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi plug rated 16 A / 3680 W, with Bluetooth used only for setup. Energy use, history and bill estimates show in the Tapo app; firmware 1.3.2 added Matter energy reporting, which TP-Link has verified in SmartThings and Home Assistant.
caveats: There's no HomeKit mode, so Apple Home works only through Matter and needs a controller such as an Apple TV or HomePod.
Alexa needs an Echo that works as a Matter controller; Matter Tapo devices don't go through the Tapo skill.
Matter energy readings need firmware 1.3.2 or later, and TP-Link only names SmartThings and Home Assistant as verified to show them.
Home Assistant's TP-Link integration asks for your TP-Link account credentials once on newer devices.
Motor loads are limited to 1/6 HP.
